slides.heading: Properties of the Verb
bullets: A verb has five Properties:  Voice, Mode, Tense, Number, and Person.
Voice — whether the subject acts or is acted upon.
Mode — the manner of the action; Tense — its time.
Number and Person — how the verb agrees with its subject.

slides.heading: Voice
bullets: Voice belongs only to transitive verbs — it shows who does and who receives.
Active Voice — the subject acts:  “The boy wrote a letter.”
Passive Voice — the subject is acted upon:  “The letter was written.”
The passive is formed with a form of “to be” + the perfect participle.

slides.heading: Practice — Active or Passive?
slides.instruction: Tell whether each verb is in the active or the passive voice.

slides.heading: The Five Modes
bullets: Indicative — states a fact:  “Fire burns.”
Potential — tells of power, duty, or possibility (may, can, must, might, could, would, should):  “You must go.”
Subjunctive — states a doubt or supposition, often with if:  “If this be true…”
Imperative — gives a command or request:  “Go.”  “Please stay.”
Infinitive — names the action without affirming it:  “to go,” “to speak.”

slides.heading: Practice — Which Mode?
slides.instruction: Tell the mode of the verb: indicative, potential, subjunctive, imperative, or infinitive.
items: If it be true, I will come.

slides.heading: The Six Tenses
bullets: Tense shows the time of the action.  Present — now:  “I write.”
Past — before now:  “I wrote.”   ·   Future — to come:  “I shall write.”
Present Perfect — past, but linked to now:  “I have written.”
Past Perfect — before another past:  “I had written.”
Future Perfect — finished before a future point:  “I shall have written.”

slides.heading: Practice — Which Tense?
slides.instruction: Name the tense of each verb.

slides.heading: Person & Number of Verbs
bullets: A verb changes a little to agree with its subject in person and number.
“I write,” but “he writes.”   ·   “The boy runs,” but “the boys run.”
A singular subject takes a singular verb; a plural subject, a plural verb.
The infinitive has no subject, so it has neither person nor number.

slides.heading: Practice — Make the Verb Agree
slides.instruction: Choose the verb form that agrees with the subject.

items: What does the potential mode express?
A verb must agree with its subject in what?
answers: The form showing whether the subject acts or is acted upon.
Indicative, subjunctive, potential, imperative, and infinitive.
